*   **Memory Complexity:** Significant reduction in storage space [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that there is a significant reduction in storage space. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly confirm this, citing specific savings of ~40% and ~90% in storage space depending on the level of coarsening. The methods described (fusing voxels, treating blocks as identical based on tolerance) match the claim's context.

Tolerance-based Voxel Fusion is a performance optimization strategy that renders volume data at variable resolutions across the spatial domain by fusing voxels with similar values [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that Tolerance-based Voxel Fusion is a performance optimization strategy that renders volume data at variable resolutions across the spatial domain by fusing voxels with similar values. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describe this strategy: they mention improving performance by rendering data at different resolutions in different areas of the spatial domain, coarsening done by fusing voxels with high tolerance values, and treating blocks of voxels identically if the difference between max and min values is under a user-specified tolerance. The evidence fully supports every fact in the claim.

It differs from image-space skipping, which creates blocky artifacts, by operating in the spatial domain to maintain visual continuity [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from image-space skipping (which creates blocky artifacts) by operating in the spatial domain to maintain visual continuity. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Skipping pixels in image space (Fig 4b) creates blocky patterns that hamper perception. Coarsening in the spatial domain (Fig 4c) is visually indistinguishable from regular rendering (Fig 4a).' This confirms that image-space skipping causes blocky artifacts, the method operates in the spatial domain, and it maintains visual continuity (being indistinguishable from regular rendering). Source [S2] provides identical information.
